result.title: SPARS: A Stability-Plasticity-Aware Region Selection Framework for Continual Learning
result.summary: Continual learning aims to acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned knowledge. However, updating shared parameters when learning new tasks often overwrites existing knowledge, causing catastrophic forgetting. Memory replay methods mitigate catastrophic forgetting but rely on previous samples, raising privacy, memory, and scalability concerns. On the other hand, parameter isolation-based methods preserve learned knowledge but may limit knowledge transfer, whereas regularization promotes adaptability but remains susceptible to interference between old and new tasks. To maintain the stability-plasticity trade-off, this paper proposes Stability-Plasticity-Aware Region Selection (SPARS), a replay-free hybrid framework combining global parameter isolation with localized parameter regularization. SPARS estimates parameter importance using either the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) or a novel Confidence Score (CS) estimator that leverages logit sensitivity and achieves comparable performance to FIM without requiring labelled data. Based on parameter importance, SPARS partitions parameters into three importance-aware regions namely, winning, neighboring, and non-important parameter regions. Each region receives a different adaptation strategy: selective freezing, soft regularization, or unrestricted learning based on its role in the stability-plasticity trade-off. To mitigate classifier bias in class-incremental learning, we employ Quadratic Discriminant Analysis to improve performance on previously learned classes .Experiments on CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet demonstrate consistent improvement in average incremental accuracy over existing isolation- and regularization-based methods across task- and class-incremental learning. On TinyImageNet, SPARS achieves the best performance with 6% improvement for class-incremental learning while retaining over 60% of parameters for future tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 面向持续学习提出无需回放的混合框架 SPARS：以 Fisher 信息矩阵或新的无标签「置信度分数」（基于 logit 敏感度）估计参数重要性，将参数划为获胜、邻近与非重要三类区域，分别施以选择性冻结、软正则与自由学习，并用二次判别分析缓解类别增量下的分类器偏置。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按重要性分区、差异化更新参数」的机制可为 latent 推理训练中的贡献分配与容量分配提供借鉴线索，尤其是无标签的 logit 敏感度估计能否充当 latent 轨迹的监督权重，可供核查。
